content.text:
I think two phases are present: NaHoO2 (mp-755141) as the main one and CaAl2O4 (mp-558636) as a minor one. I'm fairly unsure about the CaAl2O4.

- **NaHoO2 (mp-755141):** its simulated pattern matches the main observed peaks, but the whole observed pattern sits about 1.5% higher in angle (consistent with a slightly smaller cell). Observed peaks (relative intensity) at 21.4° (100), 32.95° (72), 35.2° (37), 39.65° (42), 49.0° (15), 52.5° (22) and 54.1° (38) all line up with it after that shift.
- **Peaks NaHoO2 doesn't explain:** there are small but real-looking peaks at 12.7° (about 20), 28.65° (about 16) and 30.05° (about 21). There is also an extra peak at 46.15° (about 23), and the 45.5° peak is stronger than NaHoO2 alone predicts (48 against roughly 27).
- **Why CaAl2O4:** its simulated pattern has its first peak at exactly 12.7°. From its cell I also expect peaks near 28.5° and 29.95°, and its strongest cluster appears to fall around 45.5–46°. Taken together, that covers all the extra features. None of the other seven candidates fits: either their main peaks are missing from the data, or their first peaks are in the wrong place.
- **Why the CaAl2O4 is uncertain:** a peak it predicts near 26.7°, which should be clearly visible, is barely there. Its strongest peak could also sit near 48°, where almost nothing is seen. I placed its strong peaks mostly from estimated peak spacings rather than exact positions, so a single weak NaHoO2 phase plus noise can't be ruled out.

{"present": ["mp-755141", "mp-558636"], "confidence": 0.6, "note": "NaHoO2 explains all the major peaks with a uniform shift of about 1.5%, and weak extra peaks at 12.7, 28.65, 30.05 and about 46 degrees point to minor CaAl2O4, though some of its predicted peaks are weak or missing."}
